verifications.note: Chesapeake Climate Action Network campaign page on the project. It says Virginia Natural Gas called it the Header Improvement Project, and the group called it the Header Injustice Project. It lists three new 30 inch pipelines totaling 24 miles: the Transco Interconnect Pipeline, 6.2 miles in Fauquier and Prince William counties; the Quantico Parallel Pipeline, 3.3 miles in Fauquier County; and the Mechanicsville Parallel Pipeline, 14.6 miles in Hanover, New Kent and Charles City counties. It also lists three compressor stations.

Bay Journal article from December 10, 2020. It says the State Corporation Commission dismissed Virginia Natural Gas's application for the $346 million Header Improvement Project on December 1, 2020. The project would have added 24 miles of 30 inch pipe from Prince William County south to the city of Chesapeake.

Prince William Times article from December 23, 2019. It says Virginia Natural Gas filed its application on December 6, 2019, with 30 inch pipe, a total estimated cost of $346 million and a desired in-service date of December 31, 2022.

Virginia Natural Gas press release from December 2020. It says the Commission issued an order on December 1 dismissing the company's application for the Header Improvement Project, and announces the smaller VNG Interconnect in its place.

candidates.researcher_notes: Virginia Natural Gas filed for the Header Improvement Project with the State Corporation Commission on December 6, 2019, according to a Prince William Times article from December 2019. It was three new 30 inch pipelines, 24 miles in all, plus three compressor stations, at a cost of $346 million. It ran from Prince William County through Fauquier County and on to Hanover, New Kent and Charles City counties, mainly to supply the planned C4GT gas plant in Charles City County. The Commission dismissed the application on December 1, 2020, because the conditions it had set were not met. A Bay Journal article from December 2020 and Virginia Natural Gas's own press release both report this. The company then filed the smaller VNG Interconnect, which is a separate row (P5990). That project was withdrawn in 2021. The sheet had filed both projects as one row, with the Header Improvement Project's length, cost and route under the VNG Interconnect. Capacity for this project was not found, so none is entered. The route stays not mapped until the staged route is applied. Other names: the Chesapeake Climate Action Network page uses Header Injustice Project word for word, and the Bay Journal article uses HIP. These sources are named here only and are not written to any ref cell.
